title: Redwood POC scoping with Lakemont Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for Lakemont's pilot. Customer requires SOC 2 / ISO attestation, SAML SSO + SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, 1yr audit log retention, and options for Dedicated or Private deployment to keep PII/PHI controlled. Agreed to 2-week benchmark window and deliverables listed in action items.
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll just do quick intros and then jump into the security requirements and the scope for the pilot.
[00:08] Janelle (CISO): Hi, Janelle Park, CISO at Lakemont Health. We're focused on ensuring no PHI leaks and that we meet audit requirements.
[00:15] Tom (CTO): Tom Hsu here — overseeing platform and infra, short on time so we'll focus on must-haves.
[00:21] Renee (DevOps): Renee Lopez, DevOps manager, I'll help on provisioning and logs.
[00:26] Samir (Compliance): Samir Patel, compliance — SOC 2 + ISO controls are table stakes for us.
[00:31] Aisha: Great. Marcelo from our SE team will run through the technical ask, especially the benchmark and deployment options. Marcelo?
[00:38] Marcelo (SE): Thanks Aisha. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, and security controls — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption, KMS.
[00:48] Marcelo: First, success criteria — Lakemont told us earlier they need p50 latency under 200ms for short queries (approx 64 tokens), sustained throughput of ~40 reqs/sec for core workflows, and accuracy/quality comparable to their current baseline model. Also strict no-PII egress and auditability. Is that still correct?
[01:06] Janelle: Yes that's right. And an explicit requirement: we need to be able to verify there is no model output with PHI/SSNs — either via local redaction or a post-filtering check.
[01:16] Marcelo: Understood. For the pilot we propose running two bench variants: hosted Redwood API with private network peering and a Dedicated cluster (reserved capacity) in our US-East region. That lets you compare unit costs and latencies.
[01:29] Renee: From infra side, we need SAML SSO with Okta plus SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role separation (admins, app engineers, auditors). We also need audit logs shipped to our SIEM for 1 year.
[01:41] Marcelo: Ok, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. For audit logs we can stream to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) or provide log exports; retention on Redwood side is configurable but for Private/Dedicated pilots we can keep full logs per your policy.
[01:55] Samir: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certifications? We need attestation and scope. Also vendor KMS/HSM details and key custody — do you offer customer-managed keys?
[02:07] Aisha: Yes, we can share SOC 2 and ISO27001 attestations and our security whitepaper. For encryption we support AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, and we offer KMS integrations — customer-managed keys (CMK) with major cloud KMS and HSM options for Private deployments.
[02:24] Tom: Data residency: we need to keep data in US-only regions for this pilot and ideally in our own VPC if possible.
[02:32] Marcelo: For Dedicated we can provision in US-East, and for Private we can do customer VPC/on-prem. Both preserve residency — hosted + peering is trickier re: compliance but doable with private peering and contract terms.
[02:45] Renee: About workload sizing — our baseline is 4 services hitting the endpoint: triage-bot (40 qps), discharge summarization (8 qps), search embeddings (30 qps batched), and clinical QA (5 qps). Peak concurrency could be up to 120 concurrent sessions during morning rounds.
[03:03] Marcelo: Good — we'll ask for sample traces, token distributions per request, and a 48hr traffic snapshot. That will let us size batchers, KV cache configuration, and whether quantized model variants are suitable.
[03:15] Janelle: Also we need to know what logs we get — per-token cost breakdown is interesting but we need audit trails that show who invoked what and what the input/output were, masked or hashed per PII policy.
[03:27] Marcelo: We can surface token-level cost + latency traces. For audit trails we can export request metadata, user identity (from SAML assertions), timestamps, and redacted input/output. We can also attach a hash of the payload if you prefer not to store plaintext output on Redwood side.
[03:45] Samir: Retention policy: 1 year of detailed logs, then aggregated summary for another 4 years. Can you support that lifecycle?
[03:53] Aisha: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can set retention windows and exports. For hosted plans we have default retention windows but we can augment for enterprise pilots under contract.
[04:05] Marcelo: On benchmarks — propose 2-week pilot: week 1 provisioning + smoke test + SAML integration; week 2 full load benchmarks + quality evals and security review. We'll run both hosted-private variants side-by-side if you want.
[04:20] Renee: For the benchmark runs we need the runbook, expected test harness (concurrency, token lengths), and a cost estimate so infra can approve the reserved capacity.
[04:30] Marcelo: We'll provide a benchmark runbook, puppeteer-style harness for synthetic traffic, and example scripts to replay traces you give us. We'll also include quantization profiles and expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
[04:45] Tom: Who will have admin access during the pilot? We want separation: Redwood SE + our SREs, audit-only accounts for compliance.
[04:53] Marcelo: We'll configure RBAC roles: org-admin (Redwood + customer admins as agreed), dev (app engineers), auditor (read-only logs), se (support with scoped access). SCIM can provision these roles.
[05:05] Janelle: One more: we need to validate isolation — KV cache semantics — we need to ensure no cross-tenant leakage, and that cache keys are namespace-isolated.
[05:13] Marcelo: Definitely. Our serving runtime namespaces KV cache per customer and model instance; for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee physical separation at the pool level. I'll include a short technical note showing our cache isolation approach.
[05:26] Aisha: Let's talk deliverables: Marcelo will share the benchmark runbook and cost estimate; I'll send SOC 2 and ISO attestations; Renee will provide workload traces; Lakemont will confirm SSO test Okta tenant.
[05:39] Samir: Do you do red-team style evals for prompt injection and data exfil? We need to surface adversarial tests in the pilot.
[05:47] Marcelo: We can run basic prompt-injection checks and include a set of prebuilt tests; for deeper adversarial testing we can coordinate with our security partners or you can run your pen tests on the Private deployment.
[05:59] Aisha: Any competitors mentioned that we should be aware of?
[06:02] Tom: We're also evaluating Anthropic for hosted endpoints and a few in-house self-host options, but the primary comparison is cost/latency and compliance fit.
[06:12] Marcelo: Noted.
[06:15] Aisha: Ok let's capture action items and next steps quickly.
[06:20] Renee: Quick question — onboarding timeline: how fast can you spin a Dedicated cluster for the 2-week pilot?
[06:27] Marcelo: Typically 3-5 business days once account and payment are set for Dedicated; Private takes longer due to networking — usually 2-3 weeks. For this pilot we can prioritize a Dedicated spin-up in US-East in that 3-5 day window.
[06:40] Janelle: Good. We'll aim to provide traces by Friday.
[06:45] Aisha: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the kickoff mid next week.
[06:51] [END TRANSCRIPT]

Marcelo to share benchmark runbook and cost estimate
Renee to provide sample workload traces and PII redaction rules
